originalTitle: Bilim insanları boyunların düşündüğümüz nedenden dolayı evrimleşmediğini keşfetti
titleEn: Scientists discover that necks didn't evolve for the reason we thought
headline: Bilim insanları boyunların düşündüğümüz nedenden dolayı evrimleşmediğini keşfetti.
details: Scientists have discovered that the first animals to venture onto land nearly 380 million years ago had surprisingly stiff necks, overturning a long-standing theory about evolution.
brief: The first animals to make the transition from water to land nearly 380 million years ago may have had a surprising limitation: they could barely turn their heads.
summary: The first animals to make the transition from water to land nearly 380 million years ago may have had a surprising limitation: they could barely turn their heads. Although scientists have long believed that the evolution of necks gave these pioneering creatures greater freedom to look around, new research suggests their necks were actually remarkably stiff. The discovery challenges a decades-old explanation for why animals developed distinct necks in the first place. Rather than evolving to improve head movement, necks may have emerged as part of broader changes to the skeleton that allowed animals to use their front limbs for movement.
